title: AP and TSN report installer shortages delaying window repairs in Ukraine
summary: The Associated Press reports that shortages of skilled window installers are delaying repairs to Ukrainian homes damaged by Russian attacks. TSN quotes production manager Ihor Sydorenko and parliamentary committee deputy chair Dmytro Kysylevskyi describing installer shortages and repair delays. The desk has not confirmed it.

sources.scope: Interviews with a Kyiv resident, an installer and the executive director of a Ukrainian window manufacturers' association, plus on-the-ground observations and World Bank data.
TSN quotes window production manager Ihor Sydorenko and Ukrainian parliamentary committee deputy chair Dmytro Kysylevskyi about installer shortages and repair delays.

responses.who: Dmytro Kysylevskyi, deputy chair of Ukraine’s parliamentary committee on economic development
responses.text: TSN quotes Kysylevskyi confirming shortages of qualified window installers and surveyors, citing broader skilled-trade shortages and mobilization. He said there was no immediate universal solution and suggested temporary coverings while residents await windows.

title: Witnesses report drones and explosions around Khartoum, news agencies say
summary: Witnesses told AFP and Anadolu Agency of drone activity around Khartoum, with Anadolu reporting explosions and anti-aircraft fire. Ultra Sudan separately cited military sources and eyewitnesses describing explosions and anti-aircraft fire across the capital area. The desk has not confirmed it.

sources.scope: Witnesses in and around Khartoum.

Witnesses told Anadolu about drones, explosions and anti-aircraft fire in Khartoum. The report describes one drone crashing in a residential street without exploding; it does not confirm the destruction of homes.
Military sources and eyewitnesses told Ultra Sudan that the attack began around 2:15 a.m. and explosions and anti-aircraft fire were heard across the capital area.

responses.who: Sudanese army and Rapid Support Forces
responses.text: Neither immediately commented on the incident, according to Anadolu Agency.

title: Zelenskiy says 14 people out of contact after Russian drone strike on Kyiv region apartment building
summary: Reuters reported that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said 14 people were out of contact and might be under rubble after a Russian drone struck an apartment building in the Kyiv region. Ukrainian National News separately cited Ukraine’s State Emergency Service as saying up to eight people might be trapped and nine had been evacuated. The desk has not confirmed it.

sources.scope: Zelenskiy's post on X, local officials and emergency-service footage; Reuters reporting by Pavel Polityuk.
Cites a post by Ukraine’s State Emergency Service, which said eight people might be trapped and nine had been evacuated.
Cites Kyiv regional administration head Tymur Tkachenko and Ukraine’s State Emergency Service; reports an earlier estimate of seven people potentially trapped.

responses.text: He said part of a five-story building had collapsed, nine people had been evacuated and the fire had been contained.
It said a section of the building was destroyed, two people were injured and search and rescue operations were ongoing.

title: AP reports suspected settler arson in West Bank; Israeli police say investigation opened
summary: The Associated Press reported that Gadi Eisenkot condemned overnight arson attacks on Palestinian property in the occupied West Bank that settlers are suspected of carrying out. Israeli police said they opened an investigation into arson, graffiti and property damage at four locations, according to Ynetnews. The desk has not confirmed it.

sources.scope: Eisenkot's public statement and images posted on social media
Quotes Eisenkot and Ben-Gvir, reports statements by the Israeli military and police, and interviews a Kafr Malik resident and the head of the Deir as-Sudan local council.
Quotes Eisenkot's post on X and attributes the accounts of the attacks to Palestinian media reports.
Quotes statements by Eisenkot, Ben-Gvir and other Israeli politicians.
Attributes Eisenkot's comments to his post on X.

responses.text: According to Ynetnews, police said they opened an investigation into arson, graffiti and property damage at four locations and were preparing to gather evidence and witness statements under military protection.

According to Ynetnews, the military said soldiers and Border Police were dispatched to four locations after reports of arson and graffiti, and condemned the incidents as disrupting public order, stability and security operations.

title: Israeli police say they are investigating fires and vandalism targeting Palestinian property in West Bank
summary: AP reported that Israeli police said they had opened an investigation into fires and graffiti targeting Palestinian property in the occupied West Bank. A local activist told AFP that Israeli settlers were responsible, while the Israeli military said it deployed soldiers and police to four locations and condemned the acts. The desk has not confirmed it.

sources.scope: Israeli police, a statement by opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot, and images on social media.
Israeli army and police statements and an interview with a local activist.

responses.text: Police said they had opened an investigation into the fires and graffiti, according to AP.
The military said it deployed soldiers and police to four locations and condemned the acts, according to AFP.

title: Reuters and IFR report limits on bankers’ participation in Anthropic IPO process
summary: Reuters reported, citing people familiar with the matter, that Anthropic limited the size of some banks’ IPO teams. IFR separately cited a syndicate banker describing communications limited to a handful of bankers and reported confidentiality requirements concerning teams working on OpenAI’s IPO. The desk has not confirmed it.

sources.scope: Several people familiar with the matter and people close to the process; Reuters also reviewed an email.

A banker in the underwriting syndicate described communications being limited to a handful of bankers. IFR also reported that Anthropic requested nondisclosure agreements to restrict information sharing with teams working on OpenAI’s IPO; it did not report the six-month non-compete request.

responses.who: Anthropic, Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley

title: Atlantic reports Pentagon directive limits support for congressional visits without Hegseth approval
summary: The Atlantic reported that a March 3 Pentagon memo restricted military support for congressional visits to the U.S. Central Command area without Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's approval. AP reported that Pentagon spokesman Joel Valdez linked the denial of support for Senator Chris Murphy's visit to the directive and said continuing regional operations made the policy necessary in October. The desk has not confirmed it.

sources.scope: A March 3 memo reviewed by the reporter and a person familiar with a senator's attempted visit.
Reports the March 3 directive's wording and cites Pentagon spokesman Joel Valdez on its application to Senator Chris Murphy and its continued necessity in October.
Cites a senior Pentagon official who provided the Guardian a statement linking the denial of support for Murphy's base visit to Hegseth's March 3 directive.
Cites a senior Defense Department official who told Military Times that the denial of support for Murphy's visit followed the March 3 directive.
Reuters reporting carried by Internazionale cites Murphy's remarks to journalists and an emailed statement from a senior Pentagon official about the March 3 directive.

responses.text: AP reported that Valdez said Murphy was denied access under Hegseth's regional travel directive and that continuing regional operations made the policy necessary in October.
The Atlantic reported that a spokesperson declined to provide an on-the-record comment for its article.

title: Axios reports Democrats plan more scrutiny of immigration detention purchases
summary: Axios reports that Democratic lawmakers plan greater scrutiny of federal immigration detention purchases, including ICE's $495 million purchase of a Minnesota facility. A DHS spokesperson told Axios that the price was determined through the standard federal appraisal process using independent appraisers and a replacement-cost method. The desk has not confirmed it.

sources.scope: Interviews with lawmakers and former government officials, state and local records, Government Accountability Office reports, and a DHS statement; Axios credits KARE 11 for the earlier Minnesota sale offer.
Reports on Senator Maggie Hassan's letters to DHS and CoreCivic and a statement from Representative Bennie Thompson; credits KARE 11 for the earlier Minnesota offer.
Reports Hassan's letter and statement and a DHS response to its questions about the investigation.
Cites Hassan's office and her letters, and sought comment from CoreCivic and DHS.

Reports a congressional letter and statements from its sponsors, and cites KARE 11's own investigation and interview with Minnesota's corrections commissioner. The linked article is a republication of KARE's reporting.
Its investigations unit interviewed Minnesota's corrections commissioner and obtained comments from Hassan, CoreCivic and DHS; it cites Hassan's office for the announced investigation.

responses.text: DHS told Axios that the purchase price was determined through the standard federal appraisal process using independent appraisers and a replacement-cost method.

title: The Atlantic reports HHS could release an ultra-processed food definition as soon as next week
summary: The Atlantic, citing people familiar with the plans, reported that HHS could release a federal definition of ultra-processed food as soon as next week; Politico separately reported renewed efforts to finalize it without specifying a release date. An HHS spokesperson told Politico that work on the definition had not stalled. The desk has not confirmed it.

sources.scope: Several people with knowledge of the release plan; the broader account draws on interviews with eight current and former officials involved in the process and a draft definition obtained by the outlet.

Two people familiar with the policy discussions, granted anonymity to discuss ongoing conversations, described a renewed post-election effort to finalize the definition. The report did not specify a release date.

responses.who: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services
responses.text: An HHS spokesperson told Politico that work on the definition had not stalled.

title: AP reports Hubbard won North Carolina House race after recount; WRAL reports Foxx conceded
summary: The Associated Press reported that Democrat Chuck Hubbard defeated Republican Rep. Virginia Foxx after a North Carolina recount, bringing Democrats' elected House total to at least 258 seats. WRAL reported that Foxx conceded and said she had called Hubbard to congratulate him. The desk has not confirmed it.

sources.scope: AP election results and its race call following the recount.
Reports Foxx's and Hubbard's statements about the concession following the recount.
Reports Foxx's statement conceding the race after the recount.

responses.text: According to WRAL, Foxx said she called Hubbard to congratulate him and wished him well representing the district.
According to WRAL, Hubbard said Foxx conceded by phone following the recount and thanked her for her service and commitment to a smooth transition.
